programs.name: Strong at 70
programs.promise: Build the leg, arm and grip strength daily life asks for: chairs, stairs, the floor, the groceries.
programs.who: Adults 60+ who can stand from a chair (hands allowed) and want structured strength training at home. Every level from Rebuild to Iron.
programs.ask_first: Chest pain or unusual breathlessness with activity, fainting, recent surgery or fracture, a heart or kidney condition with symptoms, or a new hip or knee (follow your surgeon's precautions; kneeling may be off-limits).
programs.equipment: Sturdy chair against a wall, kitchen counter, stairs with a rail, water jugs or grocery bags, a folded towel. Optional: the Strong Years band kit.

checkpoints.name: 30-second chair stand
checkpoints.how: Full stands in 30 s, arms crossed (H if hands used)

checkpoints.name: Five chair stands, timed
checkpoints.how: Seconds for 5 stands, arms crossed. More than 15 s is one of the European screening signs of low muscle strength: mention it to your doctor

checkpoints.name: 30-second arm curl
checkpoints.how: Full curls, same weight each time

checkpoints.name: Floor level
checkpoints.how: 0 = chair stands only · 1 = half-kneel and back with the chair · 2 = kneel and rise with the chair · 3 = sit to the floor and rise with the chair (someone home)

checkpoints.name: Two-bag carry
checkpoints.how: Seconds carrying two bags or jugs along the counter, up to 60 s

safety.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.
safety.red_flags: Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.

segments.name: Power stands

rebuild.name: Chair sit-to-stand
rebuild.how: Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms.
cues: Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward.
Sit down slow. Two or three seconds.

steady.name: Power stand (fast up, slow down)

steady.breathe: Breathe out hard as you stand.
safety: Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.

gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.

programs.name: Back Strong
programs.promise: A back-friendly strength program to help you move with less stiffness: bend, carry, turn and walk with more confidence.
programs.who: Adults 60+ with an everyday stiff or achy back who are cleared for exercise. Not a treatment for any back condition.
programs.ask_first: Back pain after a fall, fever with back pain, night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position, numbness in the saddle area, new leg weakness or loss of bladder or bowel control: those are for your doctor, today, not this program. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: you can do this program, following the long-back rule on every bend, and check with your doctor first.
programs.equipment: Chair against a wall, kitchen counter, your bed, a grocery bag or jug, walking shoes. Optional: a resistance band with door anchor.

checkpoints.name: Morning stiffness
checkpoints.how: 0–10, first 10 minutes after getting up (0 = none)

checkpoints.name: Sock test
checkpoints.how: Putting on socks seated: easy / some effort / hard / need help

checkpoints.name: Jug pick-up comfort
checkpoints.how: Hinge a half-gallon jug from a chair seat and back, 5 times: discomfort 0–10

checkpoints.name: Comfortable walking
checkpoints.how: Minutes you can walk at an easy pace before stiffness makes you stop, up to 30

checkpoints.name: 30-second chair stand
checkpoints.how: Full stands

safety.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.
safety.red_flags: Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.
sessions.caption_footer: Chang & Sun are AI characters. Content is educational, built on published research, and not medical advice. Check with your doctor before starting new exercise.

Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain (first 30 s and before each hard block)

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.
sessions.caption_footer: Chang & Sun are AI characters. Content is educational, built on published research, and not medical advice. Check with your doctor before starting new exercise.

Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain (first 30 s and before each hard block)

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.

programs.name: Balance & Steady Feet
programs.promise: Otago-style leg strength and balance practice plus simplified tai chi, to help you feel steadier on your feet.
programs.who: Adults 60+ who want to feel steadier on their feet and more confident on stairs, curbs and uneven ground. Every exercise is done at the kitchen counter.
programs.ask_first: Dizziness or fainting, a fall with injury or head strike (especially on blood thinners), sudden new unsteadiness, or new numbness: see your doctor first. Using a walker: start at Rebuild, with both hands on the counter.
programs.equipment: Kitchen counter, sturdy chair against a wall, a rolled bath towel, stairs with a rail (optional), shoes with grippy soles.

checkpoints.name: Four-stage balance
checkpoints.how: Last stage held 10 s (0–4). Under 10 s on heel-to-toe is worth mentioning to your doctor (CDC screening checkpoint)

checkpoints.name: Timed Up and Go
checkpoints.how: Seconds, normal pace, helper beside you. 12 s or more = tell your doctor

checkpoints.name: One-leg stand
checkpoints.how: Seconds up to 30, hand hovering over the counter, each leg

checkpoints.name: 30-second chair stand
checkpoints.how: Full stands

checkpoints.name: Confidence on your feet
checkpoints.how: 0–10: stairs, curbs, getting up at night, walking on grass

safety.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.
safety.red_flags: Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.

sessions.title: Otago steps
persistent_on_screen: AI character (top-left pill, white on dark, 70% opacity)
Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain (first 30 s and before each hard block)

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.
sessions.caption_footer: Chang & Sun are AI characters. Content is educational, built on published research, and not medical advice. Check with your doctor before starting new exercise.

programs.name: Grip & Hands
programs.promise: Hand mobility, grip and forearm strength for jars, bags, doors and hobbies.
programs.who: Adults 60+ who want stronger, more capable hands, including people with everyday hand stiffness. It trains the hands you have; it doesn't change arthritis itself.
programs.ask_first: A hot, red, swollen finger joint; new numbness or tingling that's getting worse; hand or wrist surgery or a fracture in the last few months: ask your doctor or hand therapist first.
programs.equipment: A hand towel, a soft ball or rolled sock, thick rubber bands, a paperback, water bottles, a jar with a lid, grocery bags. Optional: an inexpensive hand-grip dynamometer.

checkpoints.name: Jar test
checkpoints.how: Opening a new, sealed jar: easily / with effort / need a tool / no

checkpoints.name: Book pinch hold
checkpoints.how: Seconds holding a paperback by the spine, up to 30, each hand

checkpoints.name: Two-bag carry
checkpoints.how: Seconds carrying two bags or jugs, up to 60

checkpoints.name: 30-second arm curl
checkpoints.how: Full curls, same weight each time

checkpoints.name: Hand stiffness
checkpoints.how: Finger stiffness 0–10 on waking; hand pain 0–10 after the session (pain rule)

checkpoints.name: Grip (optional)
checkpoints.how: Dynamometer, best of 2, each hand. Under 27 kg (men) or 16 kg (women) is a screening sign worth mentioning to your doctor

safety.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.
safety.red_flags: Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.

sessions.title: Heavier carries
persistent_on_screen: AI character (top-left pill, white on dark, 70% opacity)
Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain (first 30 s and before each hard block)

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.
sessions.caption_footer: Chang & Sun are AI characters. Content is educational, built on published research, and not medical advice. Check with your doctor before starting new exercise.

programs.name: Walk Stronger
programs.promise: Walk farther, a little faster and more confidently: walking technique, leg strength, stairs and gradual step goals.
programs.who: Adults 60+ who walk (with or without a cane) and want to walk more. Walker users start at Rebuild with hallway lengths.
programs.ask_first: Chest pain, pressure or unusual breathlessness when you walk; calf pain that comes on with walking and eases with rest; dizziness; or a recent fall: see your doctor first.
programs.equipment: Walking shoes, a safe route (hallway, mall, sidewalk), stairs with a rail, a step counter or phone, a tape measure and timer for checkpoints.

checkpoints.name: Walking speed
checkpoints.how: Time to walk 13 feet (4 m) at your usual pace, with a 3-foot run-up. Speed (m/s) = 4 ÷ seconds. About 5 s = 0.8 m/s; 4 s = 1.0 m/s

checkpoints.name: Timed Up and Go
checkpoints.how: Seconds, normal pace, helper beside you. 12 s or more = tell your doctor

checkpoints.name: Two-minute step test
checkpoints.how: Right-knee lifts to the tape mark in 2 minutes, holding the counter

checkpoints.name: Average daily steps
checkpoints.how: Average of the last 7 days

safety.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.
safety.red_flags: Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.

Easy week: same moves, one set fewer. Then do your checkpoint at the weekend.

segments.name: Sit-to-stand

rebuild.name: Chair sit-to-stand
rebuild.how: Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms.

steady.name: Chair sit-to-stand

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.

persistent_on_screen: AI character (top-left pill, white on dark, 70% opacity)
Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain (first 30 s and before each hard block)

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.
sessions.caption_footer: Chang & Sun are AI characters. Content is educational, built on published research, and not medical advice. Check with your doctor before starting new exercise.

segments.name: Power stands

rebuild.name: Chair sit-to-stand
rebuild.how: Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms.
cues: Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward.
Sit down slow. Two or three seconds.
rebuild.breathe: Breathe out as you stand. Breathe in as you sit.

steady.name: Power stand (fast up, slow down)
steady.how: Main version: Sit tall, feet flat, arms crossed or hands on thighs. Stand up as quickly as you safely can. Think 'pop up'.
cues: Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes.
steady.breathe: Breathe out hard as you stand.
safety: Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

strong.name: Power stand (fast up, slow down)

safety: Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain (first 30 s and before each hard block)

track_descriptions.rebuild: Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you.
track_descriptions.steady: Standard version with counter or wall support.
track_descriptions.strong: Added load, slower lowering, less hand support.
track_descriptions.iron: For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced.

gentle_day_swaps.sore_knee: Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today.
gentle_day_swaps.sore_back: Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed.
gentle_day_swaps.low_energy: Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

sessions.caption_movement_addon: Go at your own pace. Hold a counter or chair. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness, or sharp pain.

programs.name: Gut Reset with Sun Yoon
programs.promise: Twelve weeks of fiber, fermented foods and protein at every meal, climbed slowly, with 26 new recipes and weekly grocery lists.
programs.who: Adults 60+ who want to eat more fiber and protein and feel more regular, cooking Korean and Chinese home food at home. Not a treatment for any bowel condition.
programs.ask_first: Kidney disease (protein and potassium limits), a past bowel blockage, Crohn's disease or a narrowed bowel, trouble swallowing, a low-fiber diet ordered by your doctor, or warfarin (keep greens steady). Not for the ladder, for your doctor, today: blood in the stool, black stool, unexplained weight loss, severe belly pain, or a change in bowel habits lasting more than a few weeks.
programs.equipment: A kitchen, a rice cooker or pot, a steamer basket, a kitchen scale (helpful), jars for banchan.

safety_global.stop_rule: Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain.
safety_global.emergency: Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
safety_global.pain_rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
safety_global.stand_slowly: Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

segments.name: Cook with me: Soybean-paste stew with tofu and shrimp

beats.speaker: SUN
beats.vo: Every Korean house has this on the stove three nights a week. Doenjang is fermented soybean paste. If you can't find it, miso works. Don't tell my mother.
beats.ost: Soybean-paste stew with tofu and shrimp

beats.speaker: SUN
beats.vo: Stir the doenjang into the water in a pot until dissolved. Add the potato, onion and garlic. Boil, then simmer 8 minutes.

beats.speaker: SUN
beats.vo: Add the zucchini and mushrooms. Simmer 5 minutes.

beats.speaker: SUN
beats.vo: Add the tofu and shrimp. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through.

beats.speaker: SUN
beats.vo: Add chili flakes if you like. Top with scallions. Serve with rice.

beats.speaker: SUN
beats.vo: Grams, not vibes. The numbers are on the recipe card.
